metadata.title: The Pay Per Lead Model Quietly Printing $75K/Month for Agencies in 2026
metadata.author: Billy Robinson
metadata.shortDescription:
💸 Hit $1,000/day Profit Selling Leads with a Pay Per Lead Agency 👉 https://www.skool.com/pay-per-lead-nation-pro/about

All My FREE Resources: https://www.skool.com/pay-per-lead-nation/about

Get my $27 Lead Farming Blueprint™🚜🌾 👉 https://leadfarmingblueprint.com/

Most pay per lead agencies are stuck selling leads the old way — 
$100 a lead, delivered to an inbox, then waiting. The problem? 
Brokers only contact 40% of leads, barely break even, and don't reorder.

In this video, I break down the new "Leads + AI" model that's letting 
agency owners charge $150 per lead instead of $100, hit 90% contact 
rates for clients, and scale to $75K/month with just 20 clients.

You'll learn:
✅ Why "speed to lead" is killing your reorders (and how AI fixes it)
✅ The exact AI agent setup we use (Pointwise, GHL, CloseBot options)
✅ A real SMS conversation showing how the bot books appointments
✅ Who this offer is for (and who to avoid)
✅ The ad strategy + B2B funnel to land clients for $300-350 each
✅ Full math breakdown: $75K/month with $35K profit on autopilot

Want the GHL templates, AI bot framework, ad copy, and sales process?
👉 Join Pay Per Lead Nation Pro: [LINK]

Quick wins from the community:
🔥 Brock — first $1,000 in profit
🔥 Anton — new solar company deals
🔥 Gareth — $1,700 profit from the debt offer
🔥 Jordan — landed his first client

Drop a comment if you want me to go deeper on any part of this model.

#PayPerLead #LeadGenAgency #AIagents #AgencyOwner

If you're new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I'm the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It's a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I'll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Open 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything.
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time.
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked.
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months.
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal.
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses.
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com to help the many people who want to start a business online do so.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we're all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win.

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles.

Never quit,

Alex

DISCLOSURE
Information shared here is for educational purposes only. Individuals and business owners should evaluate their own business strategies, and identify any potential risks. The information shared here is not a guarantee of success. Your results may vary.

metadata.title: B2B Lead Generation Services for Local Businesses: How Agencies Get Clients in 2026
metadata.author: Smart Capital
metadata.shortDescription:
A roofing company in Ohio has five great crews, twenty years of experience, and a phone that barely rings. The owner is brilliant on a roof and invisible on the internet — until one small service starts sending him three qualified calls a week. That service is B2B lead generation, and in this video Olivia builds it from scratch: what local businesses actually buy, the services that sell (lead lists, outreach, appointment setting, landing pages, CRM setup), the four pricing models with real 2026 published ranges, how to find your first three clients, the lean tool stack, outreach that gets replies, the four qualifying questions, the weekly delivery workflow, contracts and compliance, the ROI report that keeps clients paying, the seven mistakes that sink new providers, and how the business scales.

00:00 — The phone that never rang

05:56 — Finding your first three clients

07:39 — Outreach that actually gets replies

13:18 — The seven mistakes that sink new providers

A simple one-page agreement should state the lead definition, the price, the replacement policy for bad leads, who owns the data, the notice period, and the payment terms. If a phone number is wrong or the person says they never inquired, that lead is replaced, free, within an agreed window. Put it in writing before the work starts. On compliance, the rules are not optional. In the United States, cold email must follow CAN-SPAM, a real sender address, a truthful subject line, and a working unsubscribe link. And cold calls must respect the do not call list with state rules varying. In Europe, GDPR requires a lawful basis for processing personal data. Never buy scraped lists, never email people who ask to be removed, and never pretend to be the client's employee. One approach people use is a short compliance checklist before every new campaign. Clients stay when they can see the return, so measure it in their language, not yours. The report is five numbers, leads delivered, meetings held, meetings that became customers, revenue those customers brought, and total cost. Then one division, revenue divided by cost is the return on investment. Here is an illustrative example. A client pays $3,000 a month, receives 12 meetings, and closes three of them at $2,000 each. $6,000 of revenue on $3,000 of cost, a two-to-one return. If the return falls below one-to-one, you should be the first to say so with a plan to fix the targeting or the qualification. Benchmarks help you sanity check your numbers. Sopros 2025 data put the average B2B cost per lead at $198, while WordStream's 2026 benchmarks put the average search ad lead at about $67. Judge your service on cost per customer one, not cost per lead. Now the seven mistakes that sink new lead generation providers. First, selling leads them. Always prove the system on a sample first. Second, vague lead definitions, which guarantee refund arguments. Third, buying cheap scraped lists, which bounce, complain, and can get your sending domains blocked. Fourth, sending the same generic email to everyone. Relevance is the whole job. Fifth, no follow-up system, so hot replies go cold in an inbox. Sixth, taking on clients whose maths cannot work. If their customer is worth $50, no lead price makes sense. And seventh, hiding bad results. A client who hears bad news from you with a fix stays. The pattern behind all seven is the same, shortcuts and silence. This business rewards the provider who qualifies honestly, reports weekly, and tells the truth early. So how does this scale? Stage one is you, one niche, three clients doing everything by hand. Stage two is systems, outreach templates, and one shared CRM. Stage three is people, a list builder, then an appointment setter. The alternative is productizing, one fixed monthly package per niche sold the same way to every client. The numbers work. A fully loaded in-house sales rep commonly [music] costs over $100,000 a year, while a small agency retainer is a fraction of that. The takeaway is simple. Local businesses do not need more marketing advice. They need ringing phones and booked calendars. If you can find real people with real needs, qualify them honestly, deliver them fast, and report the return clearly, you have a service worth paying for. Start with one niche, prove it with a free sample, and let the first client's results bring the second. Thank you for watching Smart Capital. For more knowledge-packed videos like this, make sure to subscribe to the channel. Take great care of yourself. Goodbye.

metadata.title: How to make $500,000 per month with a lead generation business (Step-by-Step)
metadata.author: Jakub Jablonsky
metadata.shortDescription:
Apply to join our private group here: https://insider.group

In this video, I'm giving you an in-depth look at the exact system I use to make $500,000+ in profit every month from lead generation.

We'll go beyond the basic tips and really break down the strategy and processes you need to build a lead generation business that truly scales. If you want to move past just selling a few leads here and there and actually build a repeatable, high-profit operation, this is for you.

Here's What We'll Cover:

Choosing the Right Market: Why picking the right vertical is step one for finding clients who need high lead volume. Video that explains it in detail: https://youtu.be/070eyaFXUFM

Finding & Sorting Lead Buyers:
- Understanding the different types of clients: Small, Mid-Size, and Enterprise businesses.
- Why focusing on Mid-Size ($5k-$25k/mo deals) and Enterprise ($25k-$200k+/mo deals) clients who already have sales teams is key to hitting big profit numbers ($250k+/mo).
- How quickly deals close and how long partnerships last with different client types.

Building Lead Gen Systems That Deliver Quality:
- Why standard Facebook/TikTok/Instagram lead forms often fall short for high-intent leads.
- Using smarter funnels to qualify leads: Quiz Funnels, Appointment Setting Funnels, VSL (Video Sales Letter) Funnels, and ways to generate Inbound Calls.
 - Why lead quality is more important than just quantity for keeping clients happy long-term. Check my video on fixing lead quality issues: https://youtu.be/JWIshZq_19M
- Using BDRs/SDRs (sales reps) or even AI SDRs to pre-qualify leads and increase their value.

Getting the Right Traffic:
- Using Paid Ads (Meta, TikTok, Google Ads) to get a steady, controllable flow of leads.
- Paid Ads vs. Organic (like optimizing for newer search, like GPT, Perplexity)
- Why are your Ad Creatives (images/videos) the most important part for targeting the right people and controlling lead quality.
 - My process for testing Ad Creatives: Coming up with hooks, main points, and using variations (like different voices) to quickly find ads that work.
 - How ad strategy differs between platforms (e.g., Google Search vs. social media).

Tracking Your Numbers for Growth:
 - Setting up tracking to know exactly how much profit you make per lead, which ads bring quality leads, and if your client is actually closing deals from your leads.
 - How solid tracking helps you optimize everything and keep clients paying you for years (our average is 22-24 months).


Timestamps:
0:00 Intro: 500k per month with lead gen
0:10 Picking the right market
0:36 Small Clients
1:27 Mid-Size Clients: $5k-$25k/m
2:17 Enterprise Clients: $25k/m+
3:32 Funnels comparison 
6:54 Best performing funnel
8:19 Building a system to generate quality leads
9:02 Getting Traffic: Paid Ads vs. Organic LLM Search
11:12 How to create winning ad creatives and scale
13:39 Tracking
14:23 Joining insider.group

Resources Mentioned:
- Apply to Our Private Group: https://insider.group
- Video: Ranking Lead Gen Niches: https://youtu.be/070eyaFXUFM
- Video: Solving Lead Quality Problems: https://youtu.be/JWIshZq_19M
- About me: https://insider.group/about-jakub

They are presented for illustrative purposes regarding potential scale and are not guarantees of individual earnings. Building a business of this nature requires expertise and persistent execution.

In the first episode of Cold to Close,  @ericnowoslawski  (Founder, Growth Engine X) sits down with us to share the list building workflow he's spent years refining - and the one insight that changes how you think about cold outreach entirely.

Everyone's obsessing over copy when the list was broken before they wrote a single word.

  In this episode:
 - His exact list building process, start to finish
 -  How to use relevance and personalization together — at scale
 - The copywriting principles that make prospects respond
 - The sequencer Eric runs every campaign through
 - What he's building next with Growth Engine X

If your reply rates are flat and you've already tried rewriting your copy, this is the episode that reframes the whole problem.


TimeStamp:
00:00 : Introduction
00:24 : Industries Eric targets & how he evaluates them
01:25 : What happens after Eric onboards a Client
03:50 : List Building & Email Copy
05:00 : AI Copywriting & Segmentation
06:15 : What does Growth Engine X look like by the end of 2026


🔔 Subscribe for new episodes
📩 Try Smartlead for Free: https://app.smartlead.ai/sign-up
Learn more about Smartlead: https://www.smartlead.ai 
Follow us on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/smartlead-ai/


About Cold to Close

Cold to Close is a podcast series by SmartLead that follows the full arc of outbound -  from the first prospected name on a list to a signed deal. Filmed in person, this series brings you inside the workflows, decisions, and hard-won lessons of the operators who've turned cold outreach into a repeatable growth engine.

This isn't about tips. It's about the complete picture - the ICP thinking, the data strategy, the copy philosophy, the systems behind the sequences, and the mindset it takes to build outbound that scales.

Each episode features a different expert: agency founders, top-performing SDRs, and outbound operators who've done it at volume. Unfiltered. Specific. No fluff.

If you're in the business of cold outreach - or want to be - Cold to Close is where the real conversations happen.

metadata.shortDescription:
Here's how to build an enrichment waterfall in Clay to find more emails and phone numbers from the same lead list. Even emails marked valid in Apollo often come back only around 40% valid, so stacking providers one after another lets you reach more of your market without wrecking deliverability. It's for B2B founders, agency owners, and revenue leaders who want more out of every outbound list.

QUESTIONS ANSWERED IN THIS VIDEO
- What is a waterfall enrichment in Clay?
- How do I find more email addresses for my lead list?
- Are Apollo email addresses accurate?
- How do I find phone numbers for B2B leads in Clay?
- How do I save Clay credits?
- What if I can't find a decision maker's email?

KEY TAKEAWAYS
- A waterfall pings one enrichment provider after another and stops as soon as it finds a valid email or phone number.
- Put the cheapest providers first and remove the expensive ones, so you only pay more when the cheap tools come up empty.
- Connect your own API keys for email finder tools so you spend their credits instead of Clay's.
- Cap email waterfalls at about four steps, because providers further down rarely find anything new.
- Add a Claygent step that only runs when the work email is empty to pull a generic company email as a fallback, which works best for small businesses.

metadata.author: AJ Cassata
metadata.shortDescription:
💰  Need help with pipeline? Book a free 1:1 consult and explore our done-for-you services
https://calendly.com/aj--158/intro-call?utm_source=Youtube

Want FREE access to our outbound system that's generated $40M in client revenue for my partner Harvey Le and I?

Get the workshop breaking down the system, and all of our templates + AI tools here
https://youtu.be/dN2quAuDIBQ?si=rL7BiZY6MUTRA0Fa.

Here are the three ways we use Clay to get more replies, leads, and booked calls for us and our clients. Most people open Clay, get overwhelmed by everything it can do, and quit. These three workflows are the 20% that get 80% of the results: build a bigger TAM, qualify and score your leads, and personalize your messaging with AI research. It’s for B2B founders, agency owners, and revenue leaders who want more from Clay without learning every feature.

QUESTIONS ANSWERED IN THIS VIDEO

What is Clay used for in outbound?
How do I get started with Clay?
What is waterfall enrichment in Clay?
How do I find more emails for my lead list?
How do I qualify leads with AI?
How do I personalize cold emails at scale?

KEY TAKEAWAYS

Pull leads from more than one source, like B2B databases plus Google Maps, because no single database has everyone in your market.
A waterfall enrichment checks several data providers one after another, which can raise email coverage from about 40 to 50% of your list to 60 to 80%.
Use AI in Clay to qualify leads on things standard filters can’t see, like B2B vs B2C or commercial vs residential, and have it answer yes or no so you can filter fast.
Have AI research each lead and write a personalized line, like a recent project or how their role would use your product, then send it to Instantly as a custom variable.
Connect your own API keys for tools like FindEmail, ChatGPT, or Claude instead of using Clay credits, and drop the waterfall steps that rarely find anything new.

-
I’m AJ Cassata, Co Founder of Revenue Boost. Here’s my story

~ Dropped out of college at 19 to take a door to door sales job
~ Grinded hard and eventually built big sales teams at a major construction company
~ Googled “How to make money online”, got a Tai Lopez course, and started doing freelance marketing
~ Quit my job. Started an agency. 
~ Failed. Lived in a car for 4 months
~ Eventually things started to work and made my first 10k month
~ Grew the team,  upped our offer to 10k p/month selling leads on a pay per lead business
~ Built that entire business using outbound campaigns and realized other people wanted to know how we did that
~ Started Revenue Boost in 2020 during COVID to help other B2B companies book appointments with Outbound
~ 450+ clients served by now. Partnered up and featured by some of the best brands like Instantly, Digital Marketer, Foundr and more
~ Documenting everything about B2B growth, marketing, GTM and sales on this channel

Subscribe so you can stay updated on new videos, workshops & expert interviews with 7-8-figure B2B entrepreneurs.

❤️ Get In Touch

Email me aj@revenueboost.net

Clay AI has been the buzzword in the sales world lately, but does it live up to the hype? 🤔 In this video, I dive deep into Clay AI's data enrichment and lead generation capabilities, testing if it can really scale personalized outreach for sales reps or if it’s just another overhyped tool. From setting up tables to scraping Glassdoor reviews for actionable insights, I explore the potential of this powerful tool to transform your sales strategy.

Whether you're looking to build smarter lists, enhance personalization, or just streamline your sales workflow, Clay AI might be the game-changer you’ve been waiting for. Watch as I break it all down—from first impressions to advanced use cases—and let’s find out if Clay AI is worth the $149 price tag.

🚀 Already using Clay AI? Share your thoughts in the comments! Let’s learn together.

#SalesTools #ClayAI #LeadGeneration #SalesAutomation #DataEnrichment #SalesTech #B2BSales #AIForSales

Join our weekly B2B sales newsletter - https://www.salesfeedmedia.com/newsletter

metadata.title: How to Find High-Intent B2B Leads with Clay | Topic Intent + Claygent Tutorial
metadata.author: The AI Ops Guy
metadata.shortDescription:
In this tutorial, I'll show you how to use Clay's Topic Intent Signals and Claygent to find companies that may actually need your services.

We'll build an end-to-end prospecting workflow using a fictional Salesforce RevOps consulting agency as our example.

Instead of reaching out to thousands of random companies, we'll identify businesses researching relevant services, investigate their potential needs using AI, and find the right decision-makers to contact.


WHAT YOU'LL LEARN

• Find US companies that match your ideal customer profile (ICP)

• Set up Clay Topic Intent Signals to identify companies researching your services

• Understand intent providers, scores, and monitoring

• Connect topic intent signals back to company records

• Use Claygent to research buying triggers and potential business needs

• Find relevant decision-makers at qualified companies


FIND PEOPLE + EMAIL & PHONE ENRICHMENT

Want to take this workflow further?

I've created another Clay tutorial showing how to find decision-makers, set up waterfall enrichment, and enrich their work emails and phone numbers using multiple providers.

Watch the full tutorial here:
https://youtu.be/RUMB6IlG8sY?si=gdTRww_GevKn9maQ

WHO IS THIS FOR?

This workflow can be adapted to almost any B2B services business, including:

• Salesforce & RevOps consulting

• IT & cybersecurity services

• Marketing agencies

• Software implementation companies

• Business consulting firms


The goal is simple: go beyond identifying companies showing intent and understand what they might need, why they might need it, and who you should be speaking with.


TOOLS USED

Clay | Claygent | Topic Intent Signals


CONNECT WITH ME

https://hamza-saqib-portfolio.hamza-saqib0017.chatgpt.site


I share practical tutorials on Clay, AI automation, GTM engineering, and sales prospecting. Subscribe for more!

#Clay #Claygent #TopicIntent #SalesProspecting #GTMAutomation #RevenueOperations #B2BSales

Want us to build and run your outbound sales system for you? Book a call here: https://calendly.com/romain-o/discovery-call

In this video, I walk you through the exact workflow we use to launch cold email campaigns for B2B clients using Clay, Apollo, and enrichment tools like Debounce, Prospeo, and Enrich.so.

Clay table shared in the video: https://app.clay.com/shared-table/share_0sxukr8ByariubgsxNa

👇 Tools mentioned are linked below (some give me a commission, thank you!)

Smartlead: https://smartlead.ai/?via=romain-osman
Prospeo: https://prospeo.io/?via=romain
Clay.com: https://clay.com/?via=c29822
Enrich.so: https://enrich.so/
Debounce: https://debounce.io/

If you’re new here, my name is Romain Osman. I’m the co-founder of Five Element, a growth agency that helps B2B companies build outbound sales systems. We specialize in building outbound sales systems for B2B companies. We’ve helped our clients book over 1,000+ sales meetings using cold email and LinkedIn outreach, generating millions in pipeline.

Visit https://fiveelement.co to learn more.

Connect with me on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/romainosman/

metadata.title: Lead Generation with Chris Bohn - Commercial Roofing
metadata.author: American WeatherStar
metadata.shortDescription:
In this video, Kristin Dixon, Director of the Business Development Center at American WeatherStar, sat down with Chris Bohn of True Colors Industrial, LLC from Grand Rapids, Michigan. Chris, the owner of True Colors Industrial, is one of American WeatherStar's most dedicated Platinum Elite Contractors who utilizes our Lead Generation marketing program. In this video, he discusses his best strategies for making the most out of his leads.

American WeatherStar is an industry-leading manufacturer of fluid-applied roof restoration solutions. We specialize in energy-efficient systems and products that effectively restore and protect a variety of commercial and industrial roof substrates. We proudly partner with commercial roofing contractors nationwide to provide facility managers and property owners with high-performance roofing solutions, quality workmanship, reliable service, and outstanding value.

For more information on American WeatherStar or our Lead Generation marketing program, visit our website at http://www.americanweatherstar.com.

For more information on True Colors Industrial, visit their website at http://www.truecolorsind.com.

This video was filmed in January 2020.

segments.text: Hi, I’m Kristin Dixon, Director of the Business Development Center at American WeatherStar.
We operate our Lead Generation program for our Platinum and Platinum Elite Contractors.
In this video, I sat down with Chris Bohn of True Colors Industrial from Grand Rapids, Michigan.
Chris is one of our most dedicated Platinum Elite contractors who utilizes our Lead Generation program.
In this video, he discusses some of his best strategies for making the most out of his leads.
When we receive a lead from an AWS Account Executive, we try to respond back to that
prospect as soon as possible.
If we can get back to that prospect the same day, that’s great, if not, as soon as possible.
That prospect—the conversation that they had with the Account Executive—it’s fresh
in their mind.
As soon as they hang up that phone, the prospect’s mind goes back to making widgets, selling
widgets—whatever that company does.
So they’re no longer thinking about the roof, so it’s important that we get back
as soon as possible.
If you wait a week or so, for whatever reason, and try to get back to that prospect, there’s
a good chance they’re not going to remember who you are.
Maybe they have two or three other roof quotes by the time you get back to them.
Having that opportunity…having that lead is an opportunity.
We want to act on it as soon as possible and put our best foot forward.
You know, there’s nothing more frustrating than getting this hot lead—a hundred thousand
square feet, customer says on the AWS lead report that they need roof that year—and
you call the prospect, and they don’t call you back.
You can’t get ahold of them.
It happens frequently, because once again, that prospect is running their business.
The roof is something that they have to deal with, but first and foremost is making sure
that the company stays afloat and that operating the business continues.
So, you don’t get ahold of the customer—leave a message on the phone.
Call and leave another message.
If you’ve left a couple of messages, maybe don’t continue to leave messages, but keep
on calling.
Send an email, another point of contact.
Another thing that we have done if we can’t get ahold of our contact or prospect—we’ll
call the receptionist and we’ll ask to have that prospect paged.
They want to see us, they’ve talked to an Account Executive, they want to get an evaluation
on their roof.
It’s just sometimes they’re busy doing their thing.
Don’t get discouraged, keep on trying to get ahold of them.
Usually, a couple of weeks.
We don’t put an exact number on it.
It depends.
Another thing that we’ll do if it’s somebody that we’ve tried to contact and haven’t
had success—if the salesman is in that area, stop by and see them.
We don’t generally like to do that without an appointment, but stop by and see them.
Try.
But after a couple of weeks, if we’re not able to reach them, we reach back out to our
AWS Account Executive.
And say hey, we’re having some trouble reaching this person, we wanna let you know where we
are, and so that we can communicate and then you know that we’re having a hard time contacting them.
We organize our leads in chronological order.
We also organize them by type of roof and type of system that we’re going to be installing
on the roof—or that we’re presenting.
But then, every single lead we also keep notes on, because every one is unique.
We find out through qualifying, with talking with the customer, what is their time frame?
Sometimes maybe a prospect might want a roof done that season, but they don’t have the
funds, it has to go through budgeting, it might not be until the following year.
So we organize them that way and then we also make notes, and organize each one individually as well.
We have prospects occasionally that don’t have any issues with the roof, but they know
that perhaps the warranty is up, it’s an older roof, and they wanna get an idea of
what it’s gonna take to resurface that roof.
And we will actually propose systems—recoating systems—on roofs that don’t have any existing
problems, but the economy’s good now and there are customers out there that want to prevent problems.
They’re willing to be proactive and install a system before the roof is falling in.
Obviously, we want to deal with people that are having issues so that we can solve them,
but more and more in this business it’s about developing relationships and getting
on the radar with a company, because someday, everybody’s gonna need roof work.
So, along with American WeatherStar’s marketing program, we also make cold calls.
You have no idea we’re making cold calls when you’re walking in a door on what kinda
shape the roof is in, how long it’s been since it’s been done.
But you’re getting your foot in the door and you’re leaving some information, and
hopefully someday, if you continue that, when that prospect needs a roof, you’ll hear
from them because you’ve been there.
It depends on how receptive the customer is.
We’re a roofing contractor and we’re trying to sell and…supply needs to another company.
If somebody at a company is willing to give their time up to have us evaluate their roof,
then it means enough to them.
If they’re willing to do that, we’re willing to invest the time into going out and evaluating
a roof that perhaps doesn’t have any needs at the moment.
You know, our initial contact with the prospect is on the phone.
We’re trying to call and set up an evaluation.
The best way to communicate with a customer is face-to-face, always.
It’s not always possible, but during our evaluation and during our presentation, we’re
talking to the customer.
And often times on follow-up when we think we’re getting close to that closing time,
we want to be face-to-face with the customer.
We don’t close too many jobs without being face-to-face with the customer.
A phone call is, I would say, second best in communicating.
Email, I’d say is the least because it’s not a personable way of communicating with somebody.
So we generally leave emails for exchange of information, but when it comes to follow-up,
we’re trying to call or trying to see somebody face-to-face.
When we evaluate every roof, we go up on the roof and take pictures of the roof.
We take pictures of the problems of the roof.
If there are split seams, fasteners popping…we take pictures so that we can compile those
and put them into our proposal.
Every roof that we do, big or small, there’s pictures of the problems on the top of the roof.
Most owners in our market don’t up go on the roof.
They don’t know what’s on the roof.
They may have an EPDM roof, but they look up and see a metal deck, and oh, they’ve
got a metal roof!
They have no clue.
You have to, when you present the proposal, be able to show what’s wrong with the roof.
I think you should.
So that you can present those pictures.
That’s the first thing that’s in our proposal as we open it, our picture pages.
There may be four pictures, there may be twenty, depending on the scope of the project.
We want to show the owner what we’re looking at and how we’re gonna solve the problems
on his roof.
Then we go into our scope of work, which details the work that we’re going to do, which includes
a signature page.
We also include in our proposals some information on the product, proof of insurance…which
very rarely do we have to be asked for insurance because we include proof of insurance in our
proposal packet.
These are all things to build confidence in our company.
It all boils down to faith.
There are a lot of good roofing systems out there and you have to convince your prospect
that they can trust you and that you’re going to do a good job.
Of course, references go a long way.
It never hurts to give references out.
In some cases, that prospect may know one of the references that you have.
Those are invaluable.
We try to, from the time of evaluation, we wanna
schedule a presentation hopefully within a week, from the time of the evaluation.
During our evaluation and our qualifying of the prospect—asking them questions about
how old this roof, when are they gonna do their roof, do they have the financing for
the roof, who makes the decisions for the roof purchase—we’re also scheduling the
presentation at the same time.
So we’re evaluating the roof, meeting with the prospect, and scheduling when can we come
back to present our findings with you and the proposal for your roof.
Every proposal that we present, we ask at that time, you know, where are we at?
Where are we at with our purchasing?
It’s rare that we’re actually closing on an initial presentation, but it does happen
on smaller projects.
But we’re trying to get feedback so that we can follow-up, and it varies.
One prospect may say, “Well, I have to bring this to the board.”
And we would ask, “When is that board meeting?
Next Tuesday?
Can I come and see you next Wednesday?
Or better yet, can I come next Tuesday during the board meeting and present this here, so
that your board members can see it?”
But it’s all about communication and it’s keeping ourselves up and front of that prospect
the best that we can and to keep the ball rolling.
Occasionally we’ll close a job when we present it.
My salesman has a technique that actually does work sometimes.
We present our proposal, we have a signature page on the last page, he signs it, turns
the proposal around and sets the pen down.
On occasion that does work, but closing projects—these are large projects, most of the projects that
we do are fairly large—and even though they might not seem like a large project to you,
it depends on the size of the company.
Even for a small company, a roof project is big to them.
So it takes time to close it.
It’s interesting that…I say in our company, that my salesmen will sell a job several times.
Because we generally along the way will get verbal cues or verbal approvals on the project.
It’s not signed yet, but we know that’s a good one and it’s on the way.
And maybe we hear, “we’re gonna go with your roof as soon as we get financing,”
or ”we’re gonna go with your roof next year.”
And so we’ll call that a verbal close and we’ll hang on to that closely and, of course,
continue to communicate with that customer, so that when the time comes we can get a signed contract.
And it’s not uncommon for my salesman to finally come in and say, “I’ve got this
signed contract!”
And I’ll say, “Yeah, you’ve sold it four times.”
We’ve had all these little verbal cues along the way, it’s gonna sell.
And that’s kinda how it goes, it’s incremental.
You work on that and stay in front of the prospect and eventually, hopefully, you’re
the one that gets the project.
You know, I talk about follow-up.
Follow-up is key.
Things can change in the process.
If you’ve been working along with a prospect for months on a project, and all of a sudden,
another contractor has come in.
And so now you have to resell yourself against another contractor, another system.
It’s not uncommon for managers to change.
And so really, just communication, follow-up, making sure that you’re there to answer
any questions that might come up.
We’ve had customers that have been priced on an entire roof, and when it finally boils
down to it, they can’t afford to do the whole roof.
And we’ll make a suggestion, “How about half the roof this year, half the roof next year?”
Whatever we can do to help them out.
But it really goes down to communication and follow up.
You have to continue to follow-up and communicate with your customer and your prospect.
We try to stay on the same page with American WeatherStar.
Communication is always good for us.
We’re getting cues from our Account Executive on where a certain particular lead is.
It’s also important that we give information to the Account Executives.
We’re usually emailing these back and forth if there’s an important change.
If an Account Executive hears that there’s a change, they’ll often call us if it’s
something they think we need to act on quickly.
Really, it’s just keeping that communication—you know, emails and phone calls.
You know, it’s making sure that you take leads very seriously.
We get a finite number of leads in this program.
It doesn’t take a whole lot to to extrapolate out how much it costs per lead, this marketing program.
Leads aren’t cheap.
It’s a golden opportunity to go and look and hopefully close a project with a customer
that has a need.
It’s just really important to take every lead seriously.
Don’t judge a lead.
Often times, we’ll look and say, “Oh, this one looks good.”
Sometimes it’s the one that you least expect that will come through.
So treat every lead the same.
Work every lead.
We really never call a lead “dead.”
Our leads go back 15 years right now and we continue to follow those leads.
Every year, we’ll get calls from people we presented proposals to six, seven, eight
years ago, and they still haven’t done anything.
So, you don’t want to quit any leads, you don’t want to call them “dead.”
Managers often change position, owners and buildings sell, companies sell.
When we follow these leads over the course of time, it’s not uncommon to—you had
your original contact with that prospect, and after a year you might be on your third
contact, so you’ve gotta continue following up.
You might have to continue presenting that proposal to the next manager.
The key here is to just to follow-up.
Don’t quit and just keep on following up on those leads.
We’ve been in the AWS marketing program since 2012.
There are some years where we advertise in a territory, and we might not get a sale that
year in that territory, but we’re always getting leads.
Those leads are going into our database and they’re bringing work.
We know that some of those will closes eventually, but it takes time.
You can’t quit.
We’re not selling cars, you know, we’re selling roof systems and they’re not cheap.
With these roof projects, some sell fairly quick.
People contact you and they’re ready to do that roof this year, but most of them do not.
It’s a continual effort.
You work these leads when they come in, but if they haven’t sold, you continue to contact
them—whether it’s every two months, six months, annually—but you continue to contact them.
Continue to keep your name in front of the customer.
Eventually, that roof that you looked at that needed to get done is gonna really have to get done.
If you’ve been there and you’ve been in contact with them, they’re gonna be more
inclined to work with you, because you’ve been there from the beginning and you showed
them a good system.
We see that every single year.
We have people tell us, “We’re gonna do it this year!” for three years in a row.
But we don’t stop working with them because when they eventually do [their roof] we wanna
make sure that we’re there.
In Michigan, it’s seasonal work for us.
Most of our leads come in early in the year, so my salesman is super busy following those
leads that are just coming in and contacting leads that aren’t that old.
But he’s super busy this time of year and of course our service department is too.
In the winter, we have a little bit more time.
That’s our time—even though we’re still working on leads—that’s our time to do
follow-up and do a long ago, archival follow-up on leads that go way back.
We’ll continue to call and contact leads that could be several years old to see where
they’re at in the process.
It’s amazing sometimes, you look at a roof and you think well, this roof has needs now.
But it might not get that priority from the business owner, but eventually it will.
So we just gotta keep on following-up and hopefully that time will come.
If you’re interested in becoming an American WeatherStar Approved Contractor or our
Lead Generation marketing program,
visit our website at www.americanweatherstar.com
for more information.

We have prospects occasionally that don’t have any issues with the roof, but they know that perhaps the warranty is up, it’s an older roof, and they wanna get an idea of what it’s gonna take to resurface that roof. And we will actually propose systems—recoating systems—on roofs that don’t have any existing problems, but the economy’s good now and there are customers out there that want to prevent problems. They’re willing to be proactive and install a system before the roof is falling in. Obviously, we want to deal with people that are having issues so that we can solve them, but more and more in this business it’s about developing relationships and getting on the radar with a company, because someday, everybody’s gonna need roof work. So, along with American WeatherStar’s marketing program, we also make cold calls. You have no idea we’re making cold calls when you’re walking in a door on what kinda shape the roof is in, how long it’s been since it’s been done. But you’re getting your foot in the door and you’re leaving some information, and hopefully someday, if you continue that, when that prospect needs a roof, you’ll hear from them because you’ve been there. It depends on how receptive the customer is. We’re a roofing contractor and we’re trying to sell and…supply needs to another company. If somebody at a company is willing to give their time up to have us evaluate their roof, then it means enough to them. If they’re willing to do that, we’re willing to invest the time into going out and evaluating a roof that perhaps doesn’t have any needs at the moment. You know, our initial contact with the prospect is on the phone. We’re trying to call and set up an evaluation. The best way to communicate with a customer is face-to-face, always. It’s not always possible, but during our evaluation and during our presentation, we’re talking to the customer. And often times on follow-up when we think we’re getting close to that closing time, we want to be face-to-face with the customer. We don’t close too many jobs without being face-to-face with the customer. A phone call is, I would say, second best in communicating. Email, I’d say is the least because it’s not a personable way of communicating with somebody. So we generally leave emails for exchange of information, but when it comes to follow-up, we’re trying to call or trying to see somebody face-to-face. When we evaluate every roof, we go up on the roof and take pictures of the roof. We take pictures of the problems of the roof. If there are split seams, fasteners popping…we take pictures so that we can compile those and put them into our proposal. Every roof that we do, big or small, there’s pictures of the problems on the top of the roof. Most owners in our market don’t up go on the roof. They don’t know what’s on the roof. They may have an EPDM roof, but they look up and see a metal deck, and oh, they’ve got a metal roof! They have no clue. You have to, when you present the proposal, be able to show what’s wrong with the roof. I think you should. So that you can present those pictures. That’s the first thing that’s in our proposal as we open it, our picture pages. There may be four pictures, there may be twenty, depending on the scope of the project. We want to show the owner what we’re looking at and how we’re gonna solve the problems on his roof. Then we go into our scope of work, which details the work that we’re going to do, which includes a signature page. We also include in our proposals some information on the product, proof of insurance…which very rarely do we have to be asked for insurance because we include proof of insurance in our proposal packet. These are all things to build confidence in our company. It all boils down to faith. There are a lot of good roofing systems out there and you have to convince your prospect that they can trust you and that you’re going to do a good job. Of course, references go a long way. It never hurts to give references out. In some cases, that prospect may know one of the references that you have. Those are invaluable. We try to, from the time of evaluation, we wanna schedule a presentation hopefully within a week, from the time of the evaluation. During our evaluation and our qualifying of the prospect—asking them questions about how old this roof, when are they gonna do their roof, do they have the financing for the roof, who makes the decisions for the roof purchase—we’re also scheduling the presentation at the same time. So we’re evaluating the roof, meeting with the prospect, and scheduling when can we come back to present our findings with you and the proposal for your roof. Every proposal that we present, we ask at that time, you know, where are we at? Where are we at with our purchasing? It’s rare that we’re actually closing on an initial presentation, but it does happen on smaller projects. But we’re trying to get feedback so that we can follow-up, and it varies. One prospect may say, “Well, I have to bring this to the board.” And we would ask, “When is that board meeting? Next Tuesday? Can I come and see you next Wednesday? Or better yet, can I come next Tuesday during the board meeting and present this here, so that your board members can see it?” But it’s all about communication and it’s keeping ourselves up and front of that prospect the best that we can and to keep the ball rolling. Occasionally we’ll close a job when we present it. My salesman has a technique that actually does work sometimes. We present our proposal, we have a signature page on the last page, he signs it, turns the proposal around and sets the pen down. On occasion that does work, but closing projects—these are large projects, most of the projects that we do are fairly large—and even though they might not seem like a large project to you, it depends on the size of the company. Even for a small company, a roof project is big to them. So it takes time to close it. It’s interesting that…I say in our company, that my salesmen will sell a job several times. Because we generally along the way will get verbal cues or verbal approvals on the project. It’s not signed yet, but we know that’s a good one and it’s on the way. And maybe we hear, “we’re gonna go with your roof as soon as we get financing,” or ”we’re gonna go with your roof next year.” And so we’ll call that a verbal close and we’ll hang on to that closely and, of course, continue to communicate with that customer, so that when the time comes we can get a signed contract. And it’s not uncommon for my salesman to finally come in and say, “I’ve got this signed contract!” And I’ll say, “Yeah, you’ve sold it four times.” We’ve had all these little verbal cues along the way, it’s gonna sell. And that’s kinda how it goes, it’s incremental. You work on that and stay in front of the prospect and eventually, hopefully, you’re the one that gets the project. You know, I talk about follow-up. Follow-up is key. Things can change in the process. If you’ve been working along with a prospect for months on a project, and all of a sudden, another contractor has come in. And so now you have to resell yourself against another contractor, another system. It’s not uncommon for managers to change. And so really, just communication, follow-up, making sure that you’re there to answer any questions that might come up. We’ve had customers that have been priced on an entire roof, and when it finally boils down to it, they can’t afford to do the whole roof. And we’ll make a suggestion, “How about half the roof this year, half the roof next year?” Whatever we can do to help them out. But it really goes down to communication and follow up. You have to continue to follow-up and communicate with your customer and your prospect. We try to stay on the same page with American WeatherStar. Communication is always good for us. We’re getting cues from our Account Executive on where a certain particular lead is. It’s also important that we give information to the Account Executives. We’re usually emailing these back and forth if there’s an important change. If an Account Executive hears that there’s a change, they’ll often call us if it’s something they think we need to act on quickly. Really, it’s just keeping that communication—you know, emails and phone calls. You know, it’s making sure that you take leads very seriously. We get a finite number of leads in this program. It doesn’t take a whole lot to to extrapolate out how much it costs per lead, this marketing program. Leads aren’t cheap. It’s a golden opportunity to go and look and hopefully close a project with a customer that has a need. It’s just really important to take every lead seriously. Don’t judge a lead. Often times, we’ll look and say, “Oh, this one looks good.” Sometimes it’s the one that you least expect that will come through. So treat every lead the same. Work every lead. We really never call a lead “dead.” Our leads go back 15 years right now and we continue to follow those leads. Every year, we’ll get calls from people we presented proposals to six, seven, eight years ago, and they still haven’t done anything. So, you don’t want to quit any leads, you don’t want to call them “dead.” Managers often change position, owners and buildings sell, companies sell. When we follow these leads over the course of time, it’s not uncommon to—you had your original contact with that prospect, and after a year you might be on your third contact, so you’ve gotta continue following up. You might have to continue presenting that proposal to the next manager. The key here is to just to follow-up. Don’t quit and just keep on following up on those leads. We’ve been in the AWS marketing program since 2012. There are some years where we advertise in a territory, and we might not get a sale that year in that territory, but we’re always getting leads. Those leads are going into our database and they’re bringing work. We know that some of those will closes eventually, but it takes time. You can’t quit. We’re not selling cars, you know, we’re selling roof systems and they’re not cheap. With these roof projects, some sell fairly quick. People contact you and they’re ready to do that roof this year, but most of them do not. It’s a continual effort. You work these leads when they come in, but if they haven’t sold, you continue to contact them—whether it’s every two months, six months, annually—but you continue to contact them. Continue to keep your name in front of the customer. Eventually, that roof that you looked at that needed to get done is gonna really have to get done. If you’ve been there and you’ve been in contact with them, they’re gonna be more inclined to work with you, because you’ve been there from the beginning and you showed them a good system. We see that every single year. We have people tell us, “We’re gonna do it this year!” for three years in a row. But we don’t stop working with them because when they eventually do [their roof] we wanna make sure that we’re there. In Michigan, it’s seasonal work for us. Most of our leads come in early in the year, so my salesman is super busy following those leads that are just coming in and contacting leads that aren’t that old. But he’s super busy this time of year and of course our service department is too. In the winter, we have a little bit more time. That’s our time—even though we’re still working on leads—that’s our time to do follow-up and do a long ago, archival follow-up on leads that go way back. We’ll continue to call and contact leads that could be several years old to see where they’re at in the process. It’s amazing sometimes, you look at a roof and you think well, this roof has needs now. But it might not get that priority from the business owner, but eventually it will. So we just gotta keep on following-up and hopefully that time will come. If you’re interested in becoming an American WeatherStar Approved Contractor or our Lead Generation marketing program, visit our website at www.americanweatherstar.com for more information.

metadata.author: Local SEO Made Easy
metadata.shortDescription:
Learn the complete Rank and Rent business model with Paris Qureshi in this detailed, beginner-friendly masterclass.

In this nearly six-hour Rank and Rent course, I explained how to build local lead generation websites, rank them on Google, generate phone calls, and monetize those calls through Pay Per Call networks or local business owners.

Here are the links and Tools that we used in the session

For Checking Niche Coverage and Expected Payout: 
https://leadsmart-coverage.netlify.app/

To Join LeadSmart and Get Faster Approval:
https://leadsmartinc.com/affiliate-register-rank-and-rent-with-paris/

Make Websites Using AI:
https://ranklocal.cc


This masterclass starts with the fundamentals and gradually moves into practical niche research, market selection, website creation, call tracking, monetization, and lead marketplace access. It is suitable for beginners who want to understand how Rank and Rent, Pay Per Call, and platforms such as LeadSmart work in real-world local SEO.

What is Rank and Rent?

Rank and Rent is a local lead generation model in which you create and own a website targeting a specific service and location. After the website ranks on Google and starts generating leads, you can rent it to a local business or get paid for every qualified call you generate.

Unlike traditional client SEO, you own the website, domain, content, rankings, and lead-generating asset.

What you will learn in this Rank and Rent masterclass:

• What Rank and Rent is and how the model works
• The difference between Rank and Rent and Pay Per Call
• How local SEO websites generate calls and leads
• How to select profitable local service niches
• How to evaluate demand and SEO competition
• Why beginners should target micro niches and smaller locations
• How to select services, cities, ZIP codes, and coverage areas
• How Pay Per Call networks connect leads with service providers
• What LeadSmart is and how it fits into the lead generation process
• How to apply for and get access to a LeadSmart account
• What information may be required when requesting LeadSmart access
• How to navigate LeadSmart and identify suitable campaigns or offers
• How to review LeadSmart requirements, call criteria, payouts, and service areas
• How to match Rank and Rent websites with LeadSmart campaigns
• How to use Ringba for call tracking and routing
• How to connect tracking numbers, campaigns, payouts, and conversions
• How to research competitors and analyze local search results
• How to choose domains for local lead generation websites
• How to create single-city and state-level websites
• How to build Rank and Rent websites using RankLocal
• How to structure service pages and location pages
• How to generate and optimize local SEO content
• How citations, backlinks, and other ranking signals help local websites
• How to scale from your first website to a network of digital assets
• Common Rank and Rent mistakes beginners should avoid
• Real experiences, questions, strategies, and insights from active publishers

This is not a short motivational overview. It is a practical Rank and Rent training session covering the complete process—from understanding the business model to researching an opportunity, getting access to LeadSmart, selecting suitable campaigns, creating the website, tracking calls, and earning from qualified leads.

About Paris Qureshi

Paris Qureshi is a Rank and Rent and Local SEO expert from Pakistan. He specializes in building and ranking local lead generation websites for service-based businesses in the United States.

His work focuses on local SEO, Pay Per Call marketing, programmatic website creation, local lead generation, call tracking, LeadSmart campaign access, website networks, and scaling digital assets. Paris Qureshi is also the founder of RankLocal, a website-building and management platform created for Rank and Rent professionals, local SEO specialists, and lead generation marketers.

Who should watch this masterclass?

This training is useful for:

• Rank and Rent beginners
• Local SEO professionals
• Affiliate and Pay Per Call marketers
• Lead generation website owners
• People interested in building online digital assets
• LeadSmart, RankLocal, and Ringba users
• Anyone looking for a practical online business model based on SEO

The goal is simple: choose a service and location, identify a suitable LeadSmart or other Pay Per Call campaign, build a useful local website, rank it on Google, generate qualified calls, and monetize those calls through the appropriate buyer or network.

Important: Rank and Rent is not instant or guaranteed income. Results depend on niche selection, competition, website quality, SEO execution, call quality, coverage, buyer availability, LeadSmart approval, campaign requirements, and consistent work.


Connect with Paris Qureshi: https://www.facebook.com/parisali2412

#RankAndRent #LocalSEO #ParisQureshi #PayPerCall #LeadGeneration #LeadSmart #RankLocal #Ringba #SEO

क्योंकि पाकिस्तान में आप 10 प्लंबर भी ला दो किसी को तो वो प्लंबर की ज्यादा से ज्यादा क्या 1000, 2000, 3000 की होगी, 4000 की सर्विस होगी। उसमें से वो आपको क्या देगा? तो जब हम यह काम यूएसए में कर रहे होंगे तो वहां पे बहुत अच्छे पे आउट्स हैं। यह हम आगे जाके देखेंगे। तो हम क्या कर रहे होंगे? अब मैंने आपको बताया यूएसए में हम काम करेंगे। ठीक है? तो अब हमें पता चल गया अच्छा यूएसए के अंदर हमने कोई क्या करना होगा? लोकल बिजनेस की वेबसाइट बनानी होगी। ठीक है? और कॉल सेंड करनी होगी। लीड स्मार्ट ओ अभी आपको पता होना चाहिए। अब जब भी मैं लीड स्मार्ट बोलूंगा तो आपको पता होना चाहिए यह थर्ड पार्टी है जो कॉल्स बाय करते हैं। ठीक है? अच्छा अब उसके बाद नेक्स्ट हम वन स्टेप आगे चलते हैं। हमने यह तो तय कर लिया कि हम यह काम यूएसए में कर रहे होंगे। ठीक है? ओके अब जैसा कि मैं आपको बता रहा हूं कि हमने एक लोकल बिजनेस की वेबसाइट बनानी होगी यूएसए के अंदर। अब इसके अंदर मैं क्या कर सकता हूं या मैं आगे मेरी स्ट्रेटजीस क्या होंगी या मैं कैसे लेके चलूंगा? आपका जो वेबसाइट का एक रूल है या जो लोग लोकल एसइओ करते हैं या थोड़ा बहुत उनको एसइओ का पता है। उसमें एक चीज होती है कंपटीशन। ठीक है? और एक चीज होती है डिमांड। कोई भी बिजनेस है, कुछ भी है। ये दोनों चीजें हर जगह होंगी। आपकी कोई अगर किसी बाजार में शॉप भी बना रहे हो तो ये दो चीजें आप देखोगे कि उस चीज की डिमांड है या नहीं है और वहां पे कंपटीशन कितना है। मिसाल के तौर पे हम सेंटोरस में कोई शॉप लेने लगे हैं तो ऑलरेडी अगर सेंटोरस में 10 शॉप्स 15 शॉप्स या 50 शॉप्स उसी चीज की लेट्स से मैं शूज की शॉप बनाने लगा हूं और 50 शॉप्स ऑलरेडी वहां पे एक्सिस्ट करती हैं तो इसका मतलब कंपटीशन वहां पर बहुत ज्यादा है। मुझे वहां पर सर्वाइव करने के लिए उन 50 को कमपीट करना पड़ेगा। ठीक है? और दूसरी चीज है डिमांड कि सेंटोरस में लोग शूज बाय करने आते भी हो। मैं ऐसी जगह दुकान बना लूं जहां पे लोग ही नहीं आते तो फायदा ही नहीं है। और मैं ऐसी जगह दुकान बना लूं जहां पे ऑलरेडी 50 दुकानें बनी हुई हैं। उसका भी फायदा नहीं है। ठीक है? तो यह दो चीजें हमने देखनी होती हैं एसइओ के अंदर भी जब हम वेबसाइट बना रहे होते हैं किसी चीज की तो हम यह देखते हैं कि हम जिस चीज पे वेबसाइट बनाने लगे हैं वहां पे हम कमट कितना कर रहे होंगे या उस चीज की डिमांड कितनी होगी ठीक है अभी मैं उन चीजों में नहीं जा रहा कि आपने फलाना सर्च वॉल्यूम देखना है फलाना केडी देखनी है ये देख ये चीजें नहीं देख बिल्कुल बेसिक से बिगिनर लेवल पे आसान चीजें करके आपको बता रहा हूं कि समझ समझ आ जाए। बाकी ये टूल्स शूल्स इस्तेमाल करना ये सारी चीजें बाद में आई। ठीक है? अच्छा अब मेरे माइंड में यह आ गया कि हां जी ठीक है। मैंने यूएसए के अंदर एक लोकल बिजनेस की साइट बनानी है और मुझे यह भी देखना है कि उस चीज की डिमांड होनी चाहिए और यह भी देखना है कि उस चीज का इतना कंपटीशन नहीं होना चाहिए। इन दोनों को बेहतर करने के लिए मतलब डिमांड भी हो और कंपटीशन कम हो। मैं क्या करूंगा कि मैं कोई छोटा सा एरिया चूज कर लूंगा बजाय इसके कि मैं बोलूं मैं पूरे कंट्री में सर्विस देता हूं। ठीक है? अब इसका क्या मतलब है? इसका सिंपल सा ये मतलब है कि मैं जिस क्योंकि हम स्टार्ट में आपको मैंने बताया लोकल बिज़नेस। लोकल बिज़नेस मींस कि बिज़नेस जहां पे लोकेशन एग्ज़िस्ट कर रही है। तो अब जब मैं कोई वेबसाइट बिज़नेस की बनाने लगा हूं तो मुझे लोकेशन भी स्पेसिफिक करनी है कि मैं किस लोकेशन पे करूंगा या मैं किस जगह पे अपना एक बिज़नेस बनाने लगा हूं। ठीक है? जैसे मैंने इलेक्ट्रिशियन इन इस्लामाबाद किया था तो अब जब मैं यूएसए में आ गया हूं तो मुझे यूएसए का कोई एरिया चूज़ करना पड़ेगा जहां पे मैं अपना एक बिजनेस बनाऊंगा। उस एरिया को चूज करने के लिए अगर तो मैंने उसमें कंपटीशन कम करना है तो मैं क्या करूंगा? कोशिश करूंगा ऐसा एरिया हो जहां पे बहुत ज्यादा लोग ना रहते हो। ठीक है? एक तो चीज यह है कि मतलब एक एरिया है कराची। एक एरिया है कुछ छोटा सा लेट्स से छोटा सिटी कर लो वाक कर लो ठीक है अब एक बंदा जो कह रहा है कि मैं पूरे कराची में सर्विस देता हूं तो अब उसका मुकाबला भी पूरे कराची के बिजनेस ओनर्स के साथ होगा अगर एक प्लंबर कहता है कि मैं पूरे कराची में प्लंबिंग की सर्विस देता हूं उसका मुकाबला कराची के सब प्लंबर्स के साथ होगा और एक बंदा कहता है कि मैं सिर्फ वा कैंट में सर्विस देता हूं तो अब उसका मुकाबला सिर्फ वा कैंट के एरिया एरियाज के नंबर्स के साथ होगा। तो मैंने अपने माइंड में यह चीज रखनी है कि जब भी मैं एरिया चूज़ कर रहाऊंगा तो मैंने कोई बहुत बड़ा पपुलेशन वाले या बहुत बड़े एरिया वाले सिटीज को या एरियाज को सेलेक्ट नहीं करना। ठीक है? इससे क्या होगा कि मैं अपना कंपटीशन कम कर लूंगा। और मैंने इतना कम भी नहीं कर लेना कि उसमें डिमांड ही ना रहे। मतलब कि मैंने ऐसा एरिया चूज़ कर लिया कि बिल्कुल ही वह कोई एक छोटा सा टाउन है जिसमें कोई मुश्किल से 10000 2000 लोग रहते हैं। तो उसमें क्या होगा? अब डिमांड भी उतनी कम ही हो जाएगी क्योंकि लोग ही उधर इतने हैं। तो अगर मैं सिर्फ यह कह रहा हूं कि मैं एक किसी शहर के छोटे से बिल्कुल 2000 टाउन वाले लोगों में सर्विस देता हूं तो अब मेरी उस चीज की वेबसाइट होगी तो मेरा जो वेबसाइट का एक्सपोज़र है वह भी सिर्फ उन 2000 लोगों तक ही जाएगा। ठीक है? तो मैंने यह चीज अपने माइंड में रखनी है कि जब भी मैं बिजनेस वेबसाइट बना रहाऊंगा तो मैंने एरिया छोटा चूज़ करना है। पापुलेशन छोटी चूज़ करनी है। ठीक है? अभी तो मैंने ये देख लिया कि मैंने एरिया क्या चूज़ करना है। ठीक है? दूसरे नंबर पे कि मतलब मैंने बिजनेस क्या देना है या मैंने सर्विस क्या रखनी है। जैसे मैंने ऊपर अभी इलेक्ट्रिशियन रखा था। तो अब मैं यहां पर बिजनेस क्या रख रहा होगा? हम जो काम कर रहे होते हैं वो अच्छा ये भी मैं आपको बता दूं। लोकल बिजनेस में हर तरह का बिजनेस आता है। ठीक है? जो भी बिजनेस लोकली एक्सिस्ट करता हो मतलब जिसकी कोई स्पेसिफिक लोकेशन हो उसको हम लोकल बिनेस कहते हैं। जॉइन ऑन लेफ्ट वाले। अच्छा लोकल बिजनेस में कोई भी ऐसा बिजनेस जो लोकली किसी लोकेशन पर एक्सिस्ट करता है वह आता है। लेकिन हम जो काम कर रहे होंगे वो मेजर काम कर रहे होंगे होम इंप्रूवमेंट की कैटेगरी में। मींस कि मैंने जितने भी बिनेसेस एकिस्ट करते हैं मतलब जैसे कोई कारपेंटर है वह भी एज अ लोकल बिनेस ही है। ठीक है? जैसे अह बारबर है वो भी लोकल बिजनेस है क्योंकि वो किसी लोकेशन पे एक्सिस्ट करता है लेकिन वो होम इंप्रूवमेंट में नहीं आता। होम इंप्रूवमेंट से क्या मुराद है? कोई भी ऐसा बिजनेस जो होम की इंप्रूवमेंट के अंदर उसकी सर्विस एक्सिस्ट करती हो। मिसाल के तौर पे होम की इंप्रूवमेंट क्या हो सकती है? हम पेंटिंग घर में पेंट करा सकते हैं। ठीक है? घर में हम कोई भी पाइप रिपेयर कर सकते हैं। हम कोई बिजली का काम कर सकते हैं। इलेक्ट्रिशियन आ गया। हम कोई और क्या होता है? रूफ का काम कर सकते हैं। ठीक है? छत वगैरह हो गए। उसके अलावा हम कोई एप्लायंस का काम कर सकते हैं। मतलब घर के अंदर जो अप्लायंसेस होती हैं, फ्रिज होती है, ओवन होता है, एसी होता है, बहुत सारी इस तरह की चीजें होती हैं। माइक ऑफ कर लें। मतलब के जितने भी बिजनेस आपके घर के अंदर आते हैं, घर के अंदर जैसे लॉन भी आता है। ठीक है? घर के अंदर पेस्ट भी होते हैं उनको भी। तो जो भी सर्विस आपकी लिंक हो रही होगी या रेलेवेंट होगी होम इंप्रूवमेंट के अंदर। हम मेजरली उसमें काम कर रहे हो। इसकी वजह क्या है? क्यों कर रहे हैं हम ऐसे? इसकी वजह यह है कि एक तो वजह यह थी कि जो मैंने आपको पहले शुरू में बताया था कि हम जिस थर्ड पार्टी को दे रहे होंगे कॉल्स अपनी वो मेजर होम इंप्रूवमेंट की कैटेगरी में काम करता है। ठीक है? जो कि लीड स्मार्ट था वो मेजर होम इंप्रूवमेंट की कैटेगरी में मतलब इसके अंदर जो भी सर्विज आती होंगी मेजर उसमें काम करता है। ठीक है? तो अब मेरे पास कुछ गिनीचुनी लेट्स से कोई 1820 ऐसी सर्विज आ गई जो मैं टारगेट कर सकता हूं किसी भी लोकेशन के साथ। बारिश की वजह से था ये मामला। यार माइक ऑफ कर लो ना। आई हैव 20 सर्विसेस नाउ टू टारगेट एनीवेयर इन यूएसए। फिर वही है वो पहले गाने छोड़ना है तो उसमें भी तो फिर टाइम लग जाता है ना यार ये म्यूट कैसे करते हैं भाई ये म्यूट म्यूट रखो यार बीच में फिर डिस्टरबेंस होती है वो एक मॉडरेटर बनाया हुआ है बोल खैर छोड़ो टाइम नहीं जाया करते। ठीक है जी। अब मुझे मेरे पास कुछ लिस्ट आ गई है सर्विज की जिनको मैं टारगेट कर सकता हूं यूएसए में किसी भी जगह। ये तो हम पढ़ रहे थे अभी तक थ्योरी थ्योरी। ठीक है? थ्योरी है ये कि हम कोई metadata.shortDescription:
In this live Pay Per Call workshop, I built a local lead generation website from scratch in front of 400 people. Attendees followed along, built their own sites, and got help with issues during the six-hour session.

I’m Paris Qureshi, a local SEO and Rank and Rent practitioner and the founder of RankLocal. This video shows my full process for taking a Pay Per Call website from niche research to a live domain.

We cover how to research a niche, plan the website, write prompts for GPT or Claude, and build the site using AI and RankLocal. Then we buy a domain through Spaceship, connect it to hosting on Cloudflare, deploy the site, submit it to Google Search Console, and work through indexing.

The site built during the workshop was indexed in about 10 minutes. It later appeared on page one in the 4th position for the search shown in the video. You’ll see the steps we took and the problems we solved along the way. That ranking is a result from this example, not a promise that every new site will rank the same way.

If you want to learn how I build local SEO websites for Rank and Rent or Pay Per Call, follow the process with the resources below.

videos.full_text: अस्सलाम वालेकुम जी। कैसे हैं आप सब? आज है हमारी वर्कशॉप। इसको हम पार्ट टू भी कह रहे हैं। रैंक एंड रेंट या पेपर कॉल वर्कशॉप। ठीक है? पार्ट पार्ट वन में हमने मेजर चीज जो देखी थी वह नीश रिसर्च करना या रैंक एंड रेंट होता क्या है? इसको हम डिफरेंट तरीके से करते कैसे हैं? आसिम को हम बाद में जवाब देंगे। ठीक है? डिफरेंट वेज़ ऑफ डूइंग रैंक एंड रेंट। यह पेपर कॉल। फिर इन दोनों में हमने फर्क देखा था कि पेपर कॉल क्या होता है? रैंक एंड रेंट क्या होता है? फिर हमने देखा था कि डिफरेंट नेटवर्क्स क्या हैं? इनको हम कॉल्स देंगे कैसे? फिर इनसे मोनेटाइजेशन कैसे होती है? इनके अकाउंट कैसे बनते हैं? फिर इनसे नंबर कैसे लेंगे? फिर हमने नीश रिसर्च देखी थी कि भाई हम जब एक वेबसाइट बना रहे होंगे तो किस चीज की होगी। उसमें हमने देखा था कि हम नीश रिसर्च कैसे करेंगे? कौन सी ऐसी चीजें हैं जो हमने देखनी होती हैं? अगर मैं नीश रिसर्च कर रहा हूं एज अ बिगिनर। लेट्स से मैं आज पहली साइट बनाने लगा हूं। ठीक है? तो मेरे वो क्या स्टेप्स होंगे? वो कौन से स्टेप्स मैं किस तरतीब से करूंगा कि मैं अपनी पहली वेबसाइट बनाऊं। ठीक है? रिकॉर्डिंग मेरे ख्याल से तो हो रही है। लगा तो दी है बाकी अब देखते हैं। ठीक है? तो हमने पार्ट वन में ये सारी चीजें देखी थी। फिर हमने साइट बनाना भी देखा था कि आप जीपीटी से या क्लॉड से एक साइट कैसे बनाओगे। उसकी एक ज़िप डाउनलोड हुई थी। तो हमने जस्ट अ किसी भी क्लाउड प्लेटफार्म पे डिप्लॉय किया था। ठीक है? यहां तक करके उसके बाद क्योंकि टाइम ज्यादा हो गया था तो हमने ना डोमेन बाय की थी ना बाकी सारी ये चीजें की थी। लेट्स से अब हम थोड़ा सा वापस रिवाइंड करते हैं। लेट्स से मैं आज दोबारा साइट बनाने लगा हूं। ठीक है? मैं अपने लिए एक साइट बना रहा हूं। या मैंने आज एक पहली रैंक एंड रन या पेपर कॉल के लिए साइट बनानी है। तो मैं वो कौन से प्रोसेस मेरा क्या होगा? मैं कौन सी चीज पहले करूंगा? किन चीजों का ध्यान रखूंगा? क्या चीजें मैं किस तरह से करूंगा? ठीक है? नेश रिसर्च वाला पार्ट मैं थोड़ा सा तेजी से स्किप करूंगा। ठीक है? क्योंकि वो पिछले पिछली क्लास में हम दो-ती घंटे वही देखते रहे और फिर हम साइट बना के उसको डिप्लॉय करके फिर डोमेन डोमेन बाय करके फिर उसको कनेक्ट करके फिर जीएसटी से कनेक्ट करके फिर इंडेक्सिंग के लिए सबमिट करके ये सारी चीजें दिखेंग। ठीक है? अब लेट्स से मैं आज साइट बनाने लगा हूं। तो मैंने पिछले सेशन में ये देख लिया था कि मैंने किन निशेस पे काम करना है कि किन कैटेगरीज पे काम करना है और किन पे नहीं करना। फिर मैंने यह भी देख लिया था कि मैंने मेजर कैटेगरीज पर काम नहीं करना। मैंने माइक्रो पर काम करना है। ठीक है? अब जिन जिन लोगों ने पिछली क्लास ली होगी उनको ये सारी चीजें क्लियर होंगी कि मैं क्यों कह रहा हूं ये कि या मेजर कैटेगरीज क्या है? माइक्रो निशेस क्या हैं? ठीक है? और मैंने ये सारा बताया था कि क्योंकि हम लीड स्मार्ट के साथ काम कर रहे हैं। तो हम कौन सी निशेस पे काम करेंगे? कौन सी पर नहीं करेंगे। तो ये सारी चीजें पिछली उसमें कवर हैं। ठीक है? बाकी अगर कहीं पर स्क्रीन स्टक हो जाए या यह हो जाए आवाज ना आ रही हो। ठीक है? तो चैट में आप लोग बता सकते हो। तो हम शुरू करते हैं। अब लेट्स से मैं एक साइट बनाने लगा हूं। तो मेरे पास जो निशेस थी अवेलेबल थी जो रिंगबा से मुझे पता चली हैं क्योंकि मैं लीड स्मार्ट के साथ काम कर रहा हूं। तो मेरे पास जो ऑप्शन थे जिन पर मैं अपनी साइट बना सकता हूं वह यह थी प्लंबिंग थी इलेक्ट्रिशियन थी वाटर डैमेज थी रूफिंग थी एचवीएसी थी पेस्ट कंट्रोल थी ठीक है अब ये क्यों थी ये मैं आपको ऑलरेडी बता चुका हूं। सही है? अब मेरा मैंने क्या करना है? मेरे पास ये चंद निशेस हैं। मैं क्या करूंगा? मैंने इनमें से कोई ना कोई माइक्रो चूज़ करनी है। ठीक है? मतलब मैं इन प्लंबिंग के अंदर कोई माइक्रो सर्विस देखूंगा या इन प्लंबिंग की कोई छोटी सर्विस देखूंगा। मैं इस पूरी प्लंबिंग को टारगेट नहीं करूंगा। ठीक है? यह चीजें भी मैं पिछले सेशन में बता चुका हूं। ठीक है? लेट्स से मैंने प्लंबिंग की या इनमें से किसी एक की लीक डिडक्शन एज अ माइक्रो सर्विस चूज़ कर ली। दूसरे नंबर पे जो मेरा काम था, मैंने यह करना था कि मुझे एक सिटी चाहिए। तो, मैं मैंने यह चीज आपको पिछले सेशन में बताई थी कि सिटी मैं कितनी पॉपुलेशन वाले चूज़ करूंगा। बड़ी पॉपुलेशन क्यों नहीं चूज़ करूंगा? या तो मैं सिटी के साथ जाऊंगा या फिर नेबरहुड। ठीक है? नेबरहुड मींस किसी बड़े सिटी का एक छोटा इलाका। तो मैंने आपको यह बताया था कि आपने पापुलेशन रखनी है 500 के अराउंड। तो आपने कोई भी ऐसा सिटी जिसकी पापुलेशन 500 के इर्द-गिर्द हो। 400 हो, 60000 हो, 70000 हो। वो सिटी या फिर नेबरहुड। नेबरहुड मींस कोई ऐसा सिटी जिसके अंदर का कोई इलाका। लेट्स से कोई ऐसा सिटी है जिसकी पापुलेशन 2 मिलियन है तो उसके अंदर कोई ऐसा इलाका होगा जिसकी पापुलेशन 500 हो सकती है। इसको हम नेबरहुड कहते हैं। ठीक है? 300 भी चलो चल जाएगी। 400 भी चल जाएगी। ठीक है? अच्छा। अब या तो मैं सिटी चूज़ कर सकता हूं या नेबरहुड चूज़ कर सकता हूं। ठीक है? लेट्स से मैंने सिटी एक चूज़ करना है। तो अब मैं लीड स्मार्ट क्योंकि अब मैं काम कर रहा हूं लीड स्मार्ट के साथ। अगर आप लीड स्मार्ट के साथ नहीं कर रहे तो फिर आप जिस भी नेटवर्क के साथ काम कर रहेगे उसकी कवरेज में जो भी सिटी आता होगा कवरेज से मुराद कि अगर उस एरिया से कॉल आएगी तो वो नेटवर्क उस एरिया की कॉल को एज अ लेजिड कॉल कंसीडर कर सकते हैं या मतलब उसके पैसे दे सकते हैं आपको इन सिंपल टर्म्स। ठीक है? तो क्योंकि हम मेजरली लीड स्मार्ट के साथ काम कर रहे होंगे। तो मैं लीड स्मार्ट ने जो मुझे कवरेज बताई है कि भाई अगर आप प्लंबिंग की कैटेगरी में कॉल भेजने लगे हो तो इन सिटीज में से या इन जिप कोड्स में से मुझे कॉल आनी चाहिए। इसी तरह इलेक्ट्रिशियन की अपनी लिस्ट है। वाटर डैमेज की अपनी है, रूफिंग की अपनी है। ठीक है? अभी मैं क्योंकि प्लंबिंग के साथ जा रहा हूं तो मैं प्लंबिंग की कवरेज देखूंगा। यह कहां से देखूंगा? यह भी मैंने आपको पिछले सेशन में बताया था कि आप के पास मैंने लिंक्स भेजे हुए हैं। वह ठीक है? नेबरहुड वाला सॉरी लीड स्मार्ट कवरेज वाला टूल है। लीड स्मार्ट का अपना भी है जो मेरा है वह भी है। ठीक है? उसमें से आप देख सकते हो कि आप लीड स्मार्ट विच ठीक है? यह भी टूल है और उनका अपना भी है। तो मैं इससे जाके देख सकता हूं किसी भी सिटी का किसी भी नीश का। जैसे यह नीश है। मैंने प्लंबिंग चूज़ किया है यहां पे। यह मेरे पास यहां से सिटीज आ गए हैं जो लीड स्मार्ट कवर करता है। ठीक है? अब इसके अंदर से मैंने क्या किया? 500 पॉपुलेशन वाले सिटीज में से कोई भी एक चूज़ कर लूंगा। अब ये जितने लोग आप में से जिन्होंने आज बनानी है अपना साइट बनाओगे। तो आप लोगों ने में से आप लोगों ने भी इसी तरह एक नीश अभी चूज़ करनी है। ठीक है? और एक सिटी चूज़ करना है जिसकी पापुलेशन 500 या स्केर्ड होगी या नेबरहुड। ठीक है? स्क्रीन को क्या हो गया है? यह लो मैं इसका लिंक आपको चैट का ठीक है जी। अब अब क्योंकि हम बैठ तो सकते नहीं है कि हम बैठे रहे और आप लोग पहले नीश रिसर्च करते रह। तो मैंने यह किया है कि इस कवरेज में से सिटीज और निशेस जो मैंने आपको पिछले सेशन में कॉल इंटेलिजेंस का बताया था इन दोनों की मदद से 500 निशेस फाइंड की हैं। ठीक है? आप जितने लोग बैठे हो 367 हो फिलहाल। अगर सारे भी एक-एक लो ना, तो तब भी 150 निशेस एक्स्ट्रा बन जाएंगी। ठीक है? तो ये है जी आपकी ये मैं आपको भेज देता हूं यहां पे शेयर कर देता हूं इसके अंदर यहां पे आओगे ना ये देखो प्लंबिंग में आओ ये सारी निशेस हैं ये सारे सिटीज पेस्ट कंट्रोल की अपनी एचवीएसी की अपनी है रूफिंग की अपनी है इलेक्ट्रिशियन की अपनी है वाटर डैमेज की अपनी ठीक है अब अगर कंबाइंड वाले उसमें जाओ गे तो यह पूरे जितने भी हैं इनमें से कोई भी कोई बंदा कोई भी ले ले ठीक है जैसे कोई बंदा है बेड बग ट्रीटमेंट इन डिसoोटो ले ले फिर एक ये कारपेट वाली अच्छा ये कारपेंटर भी ठीक है कोई बंदा ये ले ले मिनी स्प्लिट रिपेयर ले ले कोई बंदा फर्नेस रिपेयर ले ले कोई रूफ लीक रिपेयर ले ले रूफ इंस्पेक्शन मिसिंग सिंगल रिपेयर ठीक है ये वो सारी डिशेस हैं जिनकी कॉल ऑलरेडी आई हुई है ठीक है मतलब ये कोई ऐसी डिश नहीं है जिस पे पता नहीं कॉल आएगी या नहीं कॉल इंटेलिजेंस में से इन सब निशेस में यह माइक्रो निशेस है। इन सब निशेस में से कॉल आई हुई है। ठीक है? तो उन माइक्रो नीिशस को और जो सिटीज हैं 500 इन सबको मिला के यह एक सारा बना दिया। अब यह मैं आपको सेंड कर देता हूं। यहां पे यार एडिट में फिर पता लगे कोई बंदा ऑल सेलेक्ट करके डिलीट दबा दे अ इ बैठे रहवा फिर इसकी एक अपनी कॉपी बनाओ और बिग स्क्रीन करो और कितनी इतनी बिग स्क्रीन करूं। अब सही है। अच्छा अब ये जो लिंक है ना ये आप लोग अब इसमें ग्रुप में किधर मैं शेयर करूं यार। अच्छा यह मैंने पिन कर दी है। ठीक है। फिलहाल के लिए इधर ही वो करते हैं। अब इनमें से जो भी बंदा आज साइट बना रहा है। ठीक है? इसमें से कोई भी नीश ले सकता है वो। बेटर यही है मगर [गला साफ़ करने की आवाज़] मैं रिकमेंड करूं तो आप लोग प्लंबिंग के ही अंदर जाओ। ठीक है? प्लंबिंग में जाओ, रूफिंग में जाओ, इलेक्ट्रिशियन में जाओ। ठीक है? आउटलेट रिपेयर इनमें से कोई भी ले लो। कोई बंदा किसी के साथ मिला के खुद भी कर सकता है। अगर फिर भी सुस्त है तो इसका माइंड नीशेस में जाए और यहां से कोई भी एक चूज़ कर ले कुछ भी। ठीक है? एक नीश और साथ सिटी और साथ स्टेट भी। फाइल नहीं मिल रही। फाइल क्यों नहीं मिल रही? मैंने पिन की है ना वो। किधर गई है? [नाक से की जाने वाली आवाज़] यह है ना यार चैट में और ऐसा क्या कर सकते हैं? परमिशन में व्यू व्यू की है ना यार परमिशन किधर गई है? यह देखो कितने लोग कितने हाथी चमगादड़ सारे व्यू कर रहे हैं। 40 प्लस लोग तो व्यू कर रहे हैं। अब बेचने ना लग जाना ये पता लग जाए हमारे ही ग्रुप में लोग भेज रहे होते हैं। फलानी नीश रिसर्च की है। जी0000 की नीशेस रैंक एंड रेंट वेरीिफाइड बाय एक्सपर्ट्स। तो जिसज बंदे ने अभी साइट बनाई नहीं है इनमें से कोई भी एक पिक करे ठीक है नीश भी पिक कर ले और सिटी पिक कर ले स्टेट भी और अपने पास लिख ले जब कर लो मुझे बताओ एक मिनट है आप लोगों के पास हम नेक्स्ट मूव करें फिर आगे सर इसमें से नी सेलेक्ट कैसे करनी है? यह सब सिलेक्टेड हैं। इनमें से कोई भी एक चूज़ कर लो। जैसे यह ग्रीस ट्रैप पंपिंग शवर ड्रेन अनक्लॉग अनक्कलॉगिंग। यह नीश है और यह सिटी है। ठीक है? जैसे मैं यहां पे आपको बताया था कहां गया। चाहिए कि मुझे एक यह लीग डिडक्शन जैसे मैंने चू चूज़ किया और साथ में सिटी चूज़ किया तो आप भी मैंने तो बोला था कि आप पहले लेक्चर देख कर आए। सर्प मैंने नहीं एनालिसिस किया इसमें। लेकिन इनमें आपको सर सही मिलेगा। यह माइक्रो नीिशेस हैं। कुछ भी नहीं होता। पहले ही बना लो साइट। यह सारी रिंगबा पे अवेलेबल है। कारपेट वाली पे काम नहीं करना। बस जो इस क्लास में अभी बना रहे हैं ना उन्होंने सिर्फ इधर से ही बनानी है। ठीक है? यह सिर्फ इन्हीं में से चूज़ करनी है। जंक रिमूवल नहीं सही गराज और ठीक है शीट ओपन पता नहीं क्यों नहीं हो रही यार क्या पता लोड हो गया इसलिए वाटर डैमेज भी बना सकते हो। वाटर डैमेज की भी यहां से देख लो माइक्रो इनमें से। ये देख रहे हो ड्यू टू हैवी कोलैबोरेटर यूज़ सम टूल्स फॉर दिस स्प्रेडशीट मे बिकम अनअवेलेबल। WhatsApp ग्रुप में शेयर कर दें। अच्छा यार WhatsApp इधर लॉग इन नहीं है मेरे पास। एक मिनट ओके जी रिकॉर्डिंग हमने दोबारा स्टार्ट कर दी। खैर तो आपने इस शीट से जो भी अभी साइट बना रहे हैं। ठीक है? एक इनिशली और एक सिटी यहां पे ले लिया। इसको एक दफा सर्च भी करके देख लें। जैसे हमने लेट्स से मैंने यहां पे लीग डिटेक्शन लिया। सिटी मैं यहां से चूज़ कर लेता हूं। कोई एपोका एपी पपुलेशन है जी इसकी 65,000। ठीक है। इसको भी ज़ूम कर लेते हैं। 65,000 इसकी पापुलेशन है। नीस क्या थी मेरी लीक डिटेक्शन? ये मेरी नीश बन गई है। यह मैं आके यहां पर पेस्ट करूंगा इसमें। सर्च करूंगा। अच्छा यहां से आप इसको स्क्रॉल डाउन करो। सर्क में देख लो। यह भी ब्रांड है। यह भी सर्विस पे सॉरी लोकेशन पेज है। हेल्प आ गई। यह भी इनर पेज है। यह भी इनर पेज है। लोकेशन पेज Facebook ये भी लोकेशन पेज ये एक है अमेरिकन बल्कि ये भी वो है। या तो स्टेट वाइज़ होगी या अ होगी दूसरा नेशन वाइड। ठीक है? और ये येलो पेजेस आ गए। तो यहां आपको कोई ईएमडी नहीं नजर आ रही। ठीक है? ईएमडी मींस कि किसी ने लीग डिडक्शन एपोका एफएल को टारगेट नहीं किया हुआ। सही है? और डायरेक्टरीज भी आ रही हैं। एंड कोई भी डायरेक्ट साइट नहीं है। तो मैं इस पे जा सकता हूं। सही है? तो मैं यहां से टॉल फ्री को सेलेक्ट नहीं करूंगा। लोकल को सेलेक्ट करूंगा। लोकल मींस कि मैं सिर्फ किसी लोकल एरिया पर साइट बना रहा हूं। जैसे अभी हम सिर्फ एक ये कैल्टन सीए पे बना रहे हैं। अगर मैं बना रहाऊंगा स्टेट लेवल ये नेशन वाइड तो तब मैं टॉल फ्री सेलेक्ट करूंगा। ठीक है?
